item.title: Chaetocladius montlibanus sp. n., a glacial relict species occurring in karstic springs at the Sannine Mount in Lebanon (Diptera, Chironomidae, Orthocladiinae)
item.dc:creator: Michel Brulin
item.description: Male adult of Chaetocladius montlibanus sp. n. is described based on material collected in glacial karstic springs at the upper basin of the River Beirut (central-Lebanon, Mount Sannine, alt. 1700-1500 m). item.content:encoded: Male adult of Chaetocladius montlibanus sp. n. is described based on material collected in glacial karstic springs at the upper basin of the River Beirut (central-Lebanon, Mount Sannine, alt. 1700-1500 m). In the absence of morphological resemblance with any of the known Chaetocladius species, C. montlibanus sp. n. appears to key in a separate mono-specific group: the montlibanus-group. Nevertheless, the new species is separated from the other congeners by a combination of the following distinctive characters: clypeus trapezoidal, bearing 55 setae in 7 rows; palpomere 3 with one pointed sensilla coeloconica; anal point triangular, hyaline, bare, ending with a rounded apex; virga small, bell-like shaped; inferior volsella bilobed to large lobe-like shaped, apex rounded; gonostylus linearly elongate, posterior part rounded; crista dorsalis well developed, bearing distinct striations; megaseta typically truncate.  Remarks and some associated species are highlighted.

item.title: Chaetocladius marocanus sp. n., a new crenophilic species occurring in the Mediterranean Rif of Morocco (Diptera, Chironomidae, Orthocladiinae)
item.dc:creator: Michel Brulin
item.description: Chironomidae collected in the waterfall of Chrafate, NW-Morocco (Rifian Chain, Morrocan Rif, alt. 860 m) revealed the presence of a new Chaetocladius species: C. marocanus sp. n. item.content:encoded: Chironomidae collected in the waterfall of Chrafate, NW-Morocco (Rifian Chain, Morrocan Rif, alt. 860 m) revealed the presence of a new Chaetocladius species: C. marocanus sp. n. Based on some unusual morphological characters (shape of inferior volsella, virga and gonostylus), the new species appears to key directly in the laminatus-group of species. Nevertheless, the new species is separated from other congeners by a combination of distinctive characters: palpomere 3 with 4 spatulate sensilla coeloconica; tergite IX densely covered with macrotrichia, dorsal hump well developed; anal point triangular, bearing macrotrichia, with sharp apex; virga composed of 5 separate spines including 3 located medially and 2 S-shaped placed laterally; inferior volsella bilobed, proximal part nose-like, distal part low pouch-like shaped; gonostylus arched, crista dorsalis consists of 2 separate lobes, one large located proximally and one shorter located apically.

item.content:encoded: Male adult of Polypedilum (Tripodura) camai sp. n. is described on the basis of material collected by Malaise trap placed in a young coniferous area of a large forest (Central-W France), nearby of little temporary streams and ponds. The new species keys directly in the acifer group (as emended by Vardal et al. 2002) based on the shape of anal point and presence of two lateral setae on superior volsella. Other closely related congeners (namely: P. acifer Townes, 1945; P. falcatum Zhang et al., 2015; P. procerum Zhang et al., 2015; P. pseudoacifer Zorina & Makarchenko, 2001) are also included in the acifer-gr on the basis of some taxonomic similarities. Remarks and comments are given.

item.content:encoded: Dicranota (Paradicranota) reitteri Mik, 1882, a rare alpine species previously known only from Germany, Austria and Italy, is recorded from France for the first time following surveys conducted in the Romanche Valley (Isère) and along the Durance and Séveraisse rivers (Hautes-Alpes). The occupied sites are associated with nival or nival-glacial rivers characterised by high sediment dynamics. Insects were observed exclusively on the undersides of boulders resting on exposed gravel bars in the immediate vicinity of the active channel. Photographs of the adults and male interbases are provided for the first time.

item.dc:creator: Michel Brulin
item.description: Male adult of Heleniella reginae sp. n. is described based on material collected by Malaise traps placed along the glacial stream of Mutt (Swiss Alps, upper Rhône basin). Distinctive specific characters include in particular: anal tergal bands absent; virga composed of two long rods, thick basally fused apically; sternapodeme lacking lateral horn-like projection; anal point […]
item.content:encoded: Male adult of Heleniella reginae sp. n. is described based on material collected by Malaise traps placed along the glacial stream of Mutt (Swiss Alps, upper Rhône basin). Distinctive specific characters include in particular: anal tergal bands absent; virga composed of two long rods, thick basally fused apically; sternapodeme lacking lateral horn-like projection; anal point short and wide, with apex composed of six small lobes; inferior volsella broadly semicircular and distinctly enlarged. The new species resembles to H. assiana Moubayed, 2026. They appear both to be considered as two sister species.

item.content:encoded: Les paramètres physico-chimiques de l’eau et la faune benthique de deux bassins fermés (zones de sources et marais) du haut piémont Est du Mont Liban septentrional (B.V. Orontes, alt. 1 720 – 2 150m), ont été étudiés. Ces milieux sont oligotrophes avec des eaux naturellement alcalines (pH = 8 à 8,2). Les espèces de Chironomides et de Coléoptères Hydrocanthares et Hydrophilides sont les plus nombreuses parmi les invertébrés recensés dans les milieux étudiés. La composition de la faune benthique dépend principalement du type de sources, de la nature de substrat, de la trophie de l’eau et de la durée des périodes d’assèchement. Il apparait que l’activité humaine n’affecte que légèrement le peuplement benthique jusqu’à présent.

item.title: Heleniella crenophila and H. helenae spp. n., two new species occurring in France (Diptera, Chironomidae)
item.dc:creator: Michel Brulin

item.content:encoded: Heleniella crenophila sp. n. and H. helenae sp. n. are described and diagnosed based on material collected in two high mountainous sites: the first one in the maritime Alps (spring of Fontanalba, SE-France, alt. 1700-1500 m), the second in eastern Pyrenees (glacial upper stream of the River Têt, Massif of Carlit, S-France, alt. 2300-2100 m). H. crenophila sp. n. is described as male adult and pupal exuviae, H. helenae sp. n. is described only as male adult. H. crenophila sp. n. keys near H. ornaticollis (Edwards, 1929) and H. assiana Moubayed, 2026, while H. helenae sp. n. resembles to H. gaultieri Moubayed, 2018. Main distinguishing characters found in the male adult are: distribution pattern and number of setae on postnotum, unusual shape of virga, sternapodeme, phallapodeme, anal point, inferior volsella and gonostylus. The pupal exuviae of H. crenophila sp. n. is briefly described and illustrated on the basis of the chaetotaxy and distribution pattern of armament on sternites I-III. To date, the two discovered species increase the total number of known Heleniella species to six from France, with H. dorieri Serra-Tosio, 1966, H. gaultieri, H. ornaticollis and H. serratosioi Ringe, 1976. Taxonomic notes and comments on the ecology and geographical distribution of the two new species are given.

item.content:encoded: Ce Plécoptère était connu par le passé de quelques rivières du piémont pyrénéen comme la Garonne et l’Arize (dépt. 31), le Nistos (dépt. 65) et le Lez (dépt. 09) (Le Doaré & Vinçon 2007, Ruffoni 2024). Les dernières mentions connues des Pyrénées remontent aux années 1960 (Berthélemy 1966). Malgré quelques recherches assez récentes mais loin d’être suffisantes menées par l’Opie-benthos, ces stations historiques de B. imhoffi dans le grand Sud-Ouest n’ont pas pu être actualisées (Ruffoni 2024, Office pour les insectes et leur environnement 2025). Actuellement, la situation de l’espèce sur le territoire national est préoccupante et a motivé son classement « En danger » dans la liste rouge des espèces menacées en France (Ruffoni et al. 2025).
